focus: Fixes from review 15: StatPart_TitanMaterial on MarketValue, fromMaterial trait tracking and swap, PeekTitan thread safety, statue reapply in TickInterval
diffSource: since build 15 (2026-10-06T02:51:58Z), the last reviewed build, from the build log

findings.title: Saves from before this build never get fromMaterial set: their material traits stop being swapped out and become heritable
findings.detail: TitanTrait.fromMaterial defaults to false when the key is missing, and Hediff_Titan.ExposeData's PostLoadInit block (Source/Hediff_Titan.cs:594-604) does not migrate it. On an existing jade/uranium titan, SetMaterialInternal no longer removes the old material's traits (the old code removed them via oldTraits), and InheritTraits (Source/TitanUtility.cs:171) passes them on as ordinary heritable traits. In PostLoadInit, when the saved key was absent, set fromMaterial on every trait whose def is in TitanMaterialUtility.Ext(material)?.traits. That restores the old swap behaviour for those saves.

findings.title: fromMaterial is set after PostAdded and TraitsChanged have already run
findings.detail: AddTraitInternal(def, false).fromMaterial = true assigns the flag only after AddTraitInternal has called trait.PostAdded() and TraitsChanged(). Nothing in this mod reads the flag there today (only 3 uses), but a content mod's TitanTrait.PostAdded override will always see false for a material trait. Passing the flag into AddTraitInternal would avoid that.

findings.title: Material market value now counts toward colony wealth and raid points
findings.detail: WealthWatcher adds up colony pawns' MarketValue (WealthWatcher.cs:143). The old hediff MarketValue offset never took effect for pawns, so StatPart_TitanMaterial is the first time a tamed gold or jade titan adds its material value to wealth. It fits the intent, but it is a balance change worth a changelog line.

findings.title: A swap between two materials that grant the same trait removes and re-adds it
findings.detail: The new loop removes every fromMaterial trait and then adds the new material's list, so a trait both materials grant goes through PreRemoved/RemoveEffects and AddTraitInternal again, and discovered resets to def.visible. The old code kept traits the two materials shared.
